items.stem: In the Next.js App Router, a fetch() in a Server Component has no cache options set. By default this request is:

options.text: Cached (static) unless something opts the route into dynamic rendering
options.rationale: Correct: App Router fetches default to caching; dynamic behaviour must be triggered.
That was the Pages Router mental model; App Router caches by default.
The default caching applies in development reasoning and production builds alike for this model.

options.text: Stored in the client router cache only
options.rationale: The router cache is a separate client-side layer, not where fetch results are stored.

items.stem: Which TWO are valid ways to invalidate cached data after a mutation in the App Router? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Call revalidateTag for a tag used on the fetch
options.rationale: Correct: revalidateTag purges all entries sharing that tag.

options.text: Call revalidatePath for the affected route
options.rationale: Correct: revalidatePath invalidates the cached render for that path.

options.text: Mutate a module-level variable on the server
options.rationale: That does not touch the data cache and is unsafe across requests.

options.text: Ask the user to hard-refresh the browser
options.rationale: A hard refresh does not clear the server-side data cache.

items.explanation: Correct: revalidateTag purges all entries sharing that tag.

items.stem: Why can adding 'use client' to a shared layout component be a performance mistake?

options.text: It pushes the layout and its children toward client rendering, enlarging the JS bundle
options.rationale: Correct: the client boundary cascades to descendants, shipping more JavaScript.

options.text: It disables all data fetching in the app
options.rationale: Client Components can still fetch; it does not disable fetching globally.

options.text: It forces every route to use SSG
options.rationale: 'use client' does not change the route's rendering strategy to SSG.

options.text: It prevents the app from deploying
options.rationale: The app still deploys; the issue is bundle size and interactivity cost.

items.explanation: Correct: the client boundary cascades to descendants, shipping more JavaScript.
